about: When (contracts/calls.md): a date or a length of time, as `first` and `until` take them, and a count written with the place's digit grouping. What both resolvers (participants/src/calls.ts with translator/src/resolver.ts, and kernel/crates/resolver) must read, must refuse, and must make of each program from what this seat knows. `reads`: a text read at `now` as a date (`at`: the moment the day begins) or a length of time (`in`: seconds). `refused`: neither. `counts`: a text as a count in a currency's way of writing numbers (`zero`: nought allowed); `not_counts`: refused. `cases`: `blocks` (the acts) or `asks` (the questions back, whole).
refused: at each instalment the rating law (law-rates) sets

cases.name: a date already past is asked about, with today's date
cases.program: money(to=acc-c0003, amount="100", from=acc-city, every="monthly", first="year 1, day 1")
asks: year 1, day 1 is already past: today is year 1, day 31. Give today's date or a later one, or a length of time from now.

cases.name: what is neither a date nor a length of time
cases.program: money(to=acc-c0003, amount="100", from=acc-city, every="monthly", first="next Tuesday")
asks: not a date or a duration: next Tuesday. Please say it another way.

cases.name: a payment asked for once cannot be given a day to start
asks: A payment asked for once is made when it is asked: it can't be given a day to start. For a payment made again and again, say how often; for one payment on a later day, ask for it on that day.

asks: year 1, day 2 is already past: today is year 1, day 31. Give today's date or a later one, or a length of time from now.
